verdict_reason: All 13 tiles are one museum. The anchor is 1640413193: the courtyard sculpture built out of shattered aircraft wreckage - crumpled wings, a fin, propellers and a US star-and-bar roundel piled around a central plinth carrying a black-and-white photograph of the same monument, with bilingual yellow caption plates - which is the aircraft-wreck installation in the courtyard of the Vietnam Military History Museum in Hanoi. Nine tiles are the T-54 tank marked '843' posed against a painted backdrop of Vietnamese and NLF flags under the banner 'KHONG CO GI QUY HON DOC LAP TU DO - HO CHI MINH'; a web check confirms tank 843, the national treasure that entered the Independence Palace on 30 April 1975, is held and displayed by the Vietnam Military History Museum. The rest are the same institution's other exhibits: a US-marked UH-1 on a concrete plinth in front of a white arcaded colonial block (1641291326), a long-barrelled self-propelled gun in the outdoor park (1640414513), an amphibious armoured vehicle in an indoor gallery hung with photographs (4230152046) and an anti-aircraft gun indoors (4230154642). Nothing sits anywhere else. Caveats: three id blocks only (1640/1641..., 3506/3507..., 4230...), i.e. roughly three contributors; and note the museum moved to Nam Tu Liem in 2024, whereas these photos (Flickr ids of 2007-2010) were taken at the old 28A Dien Bien Phu site beside the Hanoi Flag Tower, which is exactly where this pin falls - so the coordinate is right for the photos but a geocoder fed the museum's plain name today will return the new campus.

photos.place: Vietnam Military History Museum, Dien Bien Phu, Hanoi
photos.evidence: Cropped and upscaled 3x: the outdoor wreckage monument - a heaped mass of torn aircraft skin panels, wing sections, a tail fin, engine cowlings and two bent propellers, one panel still showing a white US star-and-bar, arranged round a plinth holding a framed black-and-white photograph of the monument, with two yellow bilingual caption boards on stakes.

Same photographer/day as 1640413193.
